newsitem.title: JAPAN: Cossack crude output halved to 40,000 bpd -- sources.
newsitem.headline: Cossack crude output halved to 40,000 bpd -- sources.

text.p: Production of Australian Cossack crude oil has been halved to 40,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) due to problems at an Australian production facility earlier this week, equity producers based in Asia said on Thursday.
Traders at the equity producers said that cossack production had been cut to 40,000 bpd from the usual 80,000 to 90,000 bpd.
They said that the field needs a gas export system replacement part that is expected to take several weeks to arrive.
In the meantime, operators are looking to carry out temporary measures to get production back up, and sources said this was likely to take about six days.
They said that how long the field"s production remains at 40,000 bpd will depend on whether the temporary measure holds.
"We want to rig a temporary measure in six days, but we do not know how successful it will be," one equity source said.

Equal-stake partners in the North West Shelf, where the Cossack Pioneer field is situated, are units of the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, the British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd -- a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp -- Chevron Corp, the Royal Dutch/Shell Group and operator Woodside Petroleum Ltd.
